title: Needs more customised templates
body:
Great app for basic Pomodoro focus sessions, but I’d love to see more customisation. It would be fantastic if users could create and save different focus templates for specific tasks. For example, a work template with a professional background and office ambience, a study template with library sounds, and a learning template with café noise. Ideally, each template would save its own timer length, background, ambient sounds, and alarm settings so everything could be launched with a single tap instead of having to change settings every time. The app is simple and effective, but adding custom focus environments would take it to the next level.

This has put me off slightly

title: Flexible timer settings, but lacking stats
body:
By comparison to all the other pomodoro apps on the store, this is the only one that suited my needs. So why did I rate 2 stars? Let me explain. 

First of all, I’m reviewing the pro version of the app (am I the only one cringing at the thought of a timer being marketed as “professional”?). Once you pass the paywall you can adjust the lengths of you work and short/long breaks. That seems like it should be the minimum bar for a timer app, but apparently it’s a premium feature. The devs are within their rights to charge for it I suppose because no free pomodoro app on the store seems to allow easy manual time setting... Some even charge a subscription fee. So that’s where this app wins the stars - one for allowing me to set manual timers when no others will, and a second for the other more inconsequential customisation options (timer colours, timer chimes).

But I think the app is lacking when it comes to stats. You can see your average working time over 30 days or 14 days, but nothing more. It’d be better if the devs would let us enter our own time periods to see averages, because otherwise stats sections is almost pointless for the first two weeks, aside from checking your daily work time. It would be better still if the amount of time spent working each day could be represented more clearly on the focus page, rather than the stats page. At the mount you get to see how many “rounds” you’ve done. This means how many times you’ve set a timer and worked through it. But if you work through one 25min timer and then a 50min timer, that is still only represented as 2 rounds. It would be nice to have the option to change the metric from rounds to minutes on the focus screen.

All-in-all, it’s fine. It’s worth the £2 spend, only because no other apps give you the same flexibility for cheaper. But let’s face it - setting a custom timer should be the real minimum bar for a timer app. And useful features like stats should have been developed ahead of quality of life features like a chime that meows like a cat.
